members.title: Spurs winning streak driven by Victor Wembanyama, but he is far from alone
members.capturedExcerpt: Earlier this month, Victor Wembanyama, still in his uniform, sat at the podium and seemed almost disappointed. He had just made history, generating a stat line that had only been replicated one other time since 1974. His 52-point, 24-rebound, 8-block masterclass on Nov. 4 propelled the San Antonio Spurs past the Dallas Mavericks in a one-point win. But Wembanyama had been dealing with a cold, and it was only that night when he felt like he had finally gotten his legs back. “It should be more like this,” Wembanyama said. “More often.” Wembanyama was not wrong. The Spurs are the hottest team in the NBA, winners of 12 consecutive games. They’ve climbed to the top of Western Conference and are tied with the Los Angeles Lakers for best record in the NBA. San Antonio ranks within the top three in offensive rating (119.2), defensive rating (106.6) and net rating (+12.6). And one season after falling short in the NBA Finals, the Spurs are looking like a dominant team, one that could be poised for a championship run. How exactly is San Antonio doing it? Throughout it all, it has been Wembanyama carrying the Spurs. On Monday, Nov. 16, Wembanyama earned Western Conference Player of the Week, his second such honor in the regular season’s first month. He’s averaging career highs in points (28.6), rebounds (11.6) and blocks (4.3). But more than just the numbers, it’s the way Wembanyama is playing the game that is elevating San Antonio. members.title: Wizards hammered by Memphis Grizzlies for 8th straight loss
members.capturedExcerpt: The Wizards played 24 good minutes against the Memphis Grizzlies. Unfortunately, the game lasted 48 minutes. Their worst 12 minutes came in the third quarter. They started the period up 10 and finished it down 14, courtesy of a 42-18 beatdown by Cameron Boozer, Zach Edey, and the rest of the Grizzlies. Fifteen games into the season where they hoped to compete again, the Wizards have a 4-11 record, and they’re currently on an eight-game losing streak. It’s starting to feel like last year. And the year before. And the year before. If you missed this one, a) congratulations, and b) here are a few tidbits to illustrate how this one went: Washington’s defensive game plan was built around defensive indifference — they were going to concede three-point shots to Boozer. He missed his first five…and then made seven of his last eight. Boozer finished with a career-high 29 points,. Edey dominated Washington’s Twin Towers lineup, notching 23 points (on 10-15 shooting) and 10 rebounds in just 21 minutes. Javon Small had his first career double-double — 12 points, 12 assists. The Grizzlies shot 64.2% (effective field goal percentage) and rebounded 42.9% of their misses. That’s the second consecutive game the Wizards gave up a 60+% efg and an opponent offensive rebound rate above 40%. I don’t know for sure because it probably never occurred to anyone to track this combination of stats, but I suspect it’s exceedingly rare to do both in a single game. members.title: Recap: Wizards drop eighth straight with 136-120 loss to Grizzlies
members.capturedExcerpt: The Washington Wizards couldn’t hold onto a 12-point second-quarter lead Monday night, as the Memphis Grizzlies outscored them by 24 in the third quarter to pull away for a 131-120 victory and hand Washington its eighth consecutive loss. Washington opened the game with a 35-33 lead, fueled by 10 first-quarter points from Anthony Davis who connected on 4-of-6 field goals and knocked down a pair of free throws. AJ Dybantsa and Trae Young each knocked down a three-pointer, while Khris Middleton added two more from beyond the arc. Young, who went scoreless in Sunday’s game against the Houston Rockets, also dished out five assists in the opening quarter, helping set the pace for Washington’s offense. Seven different Wizards scored in the first quarter, including 15 points from the bench, and Washington shot 55.6% from distance. Washington went back and forth with Memphis to start the second quarter, but Young continued to orchestrate the offense. He added five more assists to reach 10 for the half, becoming the second player in the NBA this season to record 10+ assists before halftime. Dybantsa put together an impressive second quarter. He caught a lob from Young, threw down a put-back dunk and picked Cam Spencer’s pocket before finishing the ensuing fast break with a two-handed slam. members.title: GTA 6 is Close to 15 Million Sold and $1.5 Billion Revenue – Rumor
members.capturedExcerpt: Only days after analyst firm Sensor Tower estimated over 10 million sales for Grand Theft Auto 6, a new milestone has reportedly been reached. Rockstar Games’ open-world behemoth, launching on November 19th for Xbox Series X/S and PS5, has allegedly neared 15 million sales. It’s currently estimated at 14.94 million units sold, with PlayStation dominating again at 11.13 million sales while Xbox is at 3.81 million. Total revenue has seemingly topped $1.45 billion, with $1.08 billion for PS5 and $368 million for Xbox. Of course, these are estimates, as Rockstar and Take-Two have not offered any official sales figures heading into launch. The most we’ve heard from the latter is that pre-orders are “far in excess” of its expectations, though it promises to share more once the game is out there. Nevertheless, if these are close to the real total, Grand Theft Auto 6 may be close to breaking even on its reported $2 billion+ budget from launch itself. Marketing and distribution wouldn’t be included, but it’s still an incredible achievement, displacing its predecessor’s $800 million launch sales without breaking a sweat. Once it’s finally out there for all and sundry to play after years of waiting, what’s next for Rockstar Games? Thankfully, we won’t have to wait long to find out, per Take-Two CEO Strauss Zelnick, so stay tuned.

members.title: GTA 6’s Hacker Pleads Guilty To Charges Connected to 2022 Leaks
members.capturedExcerpt: Remember those GTA 6 leaks from 2022, long before Rockstar even released a trailer or officially confirmed it exists? An artist for Rockstar described them as “weirdly invasive” back then, and it looks like one of the culprits is now facing the consequences. 17-year-old Arion Kurtaj was apprehended for the crime and relegated to custody in a hospital owing to his existing medical conditions. However, he was soon deemed fit to stand trial per the BBC and has pleaded guilty to all charges against him, reportedly with no visible emotion. He is to be sentenced at a later date. It’s probably welcome news for several of Rockstar’s tireless team members whose efforts risked being undermined by Kurtaj’s actions. Well, let’s hope they put this unfortunate business behind them and bask in the admiration they’ll receive for those dynamic weather systems and everything else they’ve been cooking up for us over the last thirteen years. We spoke of not being able to believe we’re this close to playing the game a month ago, and that hasn’t really changed, if we’re being honest, even though we’re just a little over a day away from launch. members.title: Grand Theft Auto 6 hacker pleads guilty to all charges
members.capturedExcerpt: The BBC reports that Arion Kurtaj, who hacked Rockstar and dumped a massive trove of content from Grand Theft Auto 6 more than a year before it was formally revealed, has pleaded guilty to that and other hacks carried out while he was a member of the Lapsus$ hacking group. Kurtaj's hack of Rockstar was notable not for the GTA 6 infodump that followed, but because of how it was carried out: With an Amazon Fire Stick, a mobile phone, and a Bluetooth keyboard and mouse, connected to a TV in a Travelodge hotel room where he was being held under police protection because of threats against him made by rival hackers over stolen bitcoin. A 2023 assessment found Kurtaj had "acute autism" and was determined to return to "cybercrime" as soon as possible, despite the fact that he was literally standing trial for doing cybercrimes. Because of that, the jury was asked to determine if he had committed the hacks (it found he had) but not whether he had done so with criminal intent; he was subsequently sentenced to an indefinite stay at a secure hospital, where he would remain unless and until doctors determined that he was no longer a danger. As we noted at the time, "danger" might seem a bit of a strong word for someone who leaked videogame footage, but the Lapsus$ group had also hacked Microsoft, Samsung, Nvidia and UK telecom company BT&EE, and stole millions in cryptocurrency from individuals. Kurtaj was also reportedly violent while in hospital custody, causing "dozens" of reports of…

members.title: GTA VI Hacker Pleads Guilty To 2022 Rockstar Games Breach
members.capturedExcerpt: Arion Kurtaj, the 21-year-old hacker who posted tons of Grand Theft Auto VI clips online after breaching Rockstar Games' servers, pleaded guilty Monday at the Woolwich Crown Court after being arrested in 2022, according to the BBC. He pleaded guilty to all counts, including those attached to hacks at Uber and others that he carried out while a teenager out on bail (and being housed in a hotel "to protect him from rival hackers"), when he used an Amazon Fire Stick plugged into a hotel television to gain access to the clips and publish them online. In 2022, Kurtaj got into Rockstar Games' Slack to threaten to release Grand Theft Auto VI code. When Rockstar Games did not cooperate, Kurtaj posted the clips and source code. Rockstar Games said it spent $5 million to "recover from the hack, plus thousands of hours of staff time," BBC reported. The clips Kurtaj posted in 2022 were the public's first look at GTA VI and in particular its playable female character, Lucia. Kurtaj's original sentence had him held indefinitely at a hospital, but he had recently been deemed fit for trial. He'll move to a prison in January, according to the report. BBC reported Kurtaj and the hacking group Lapsu$, which he was a part of, cost the companies targeted $13 million in damages. The group also stole "at least $300,000 from individual victims," BBC said. Kurtaj's guilty pleas also included charges related to assaults on hospital workers during his custody. members.title: Netflix Lays Off More Games Workers
members.capturedExcerpt: There's been yet more layoffs in Netflix's gaming department, according to posts by impacted workers on LinkedIn. The number of cuts is unclear, and the announcements come a few weeks after Netflix previously laid off 60 game workers in late October. "Netflix Games recently went through a restructuring as the team shifts how it approaches making games, and my role, along with those of many talented colleagues, was impacted," wrote Andrew Brownell, a game director at Netflix Games, on LinkedIn. Brownell's post lists three artists who were impacted. In their posts and LinkedIn bios, these workers make reference to "unannounced" projects connected to "licensed-IP," and Brownell writes that Netflix Games worked on "cloud-streamed action games, phones as controllers, motion and microphone input, gyro and air-mouse controls, and designing around two screens at once. Alongside that, we worked on concepts for some of Netflix’s biggest franchises, partnering closely with IP owners to create experiences that felt authentic to those worlds and their fans." Making games out of its existing properties has been one of Netflix's focus with games, though in recent years that's shifted to a focus on party games that use the kinds of controls Brownell describes.
